name: foot and ankle pain overview
title: Foot and ankle pain: after a twisted ankle the Ottawa rules decide the X-ray; without injury the site of the pain separates Achilles tendinopathy and plantar fasciitis at the heel, tibialis posterior dysfunction at the medial ankle, bunion and Morton's neuroma in the forefoot, and the diabetic foot; each column gives presentation, workup and treatment

root.title: Foot or ankle pain: was there an INJURY? If not, WHERE does it hurt?
lines: almost all: education first, with a long, slow recovery expected · surgery is the exception

head: h
Ankle sprain
85% lateral: twist in plantarflexion + inversion
medial: deltoid (foot caught on turf)
pres: Swelling · bruising · pain over the ligament
• partial to full tear · all three torn → dislocation
inv: • bone tenderness: back 6 cm or tip of either malleolus, navicular, 5th metatarsal base
• cannot bear weight at once AND in the emergency department
X-ray: a sprain that is a FRACTURE
• unimalleolar: non-operative if the talus is stable
• Maisonneuve (forceful external rotation): interosseous ligament torn ± medial malleolus avulsion or deltoid rupture → surgery
tx: • NSAIDs, analgesics · bracing or taping: pros and cons

head: h
Achilles tendinopathy
runners, after a rise in training
pres: Pain at or just above the calcaneal insertion
inv: surgery vs cast or boot: decide WITH the patient
surgery: slightly fewer re-ruptures but infection, wound problems, scarring, sural nerve injury
tx: Activity change · footwear that does not press
• physio: stretching, ECCENTRIC strengthening, friction massage, shockwave
• NSAIDs topical or oral · ? topical nitrites

head: h
Plantar fasciitis
age 40-60, F > M
plantar fascia overworked: chronic insertional inflammation
pres: Anteromedial heel pain on the FIRST morning steps
tx: Heel pad · arch-support shoes · weight loss
• heel lift or wedge: careful long term
• fascia stretching · strengthen arch stabilizers: tibialis posterior, intrinsics

head: h
Tibialis posterior dysfunction
tendon hypovascular below the medial malleolus
risk: trauma, steroids, inflammatory arthritis, obesity, diabetes
pres: • flat foot: FLEXIBLE, then RIGID (dropped talus)
inv: is the flat foot flexible or rigid?
tx: RICE · physio for the arch stabilizers · orthosis
• orthosis: foot or ankle-foot · corrective vs accommodative
• NSAIDs if needed · modify risk factors

head: h
Bunion (hallux valgus)
footwear (F > M) · metatarsus varus
pres: Pain at the medial first metatarsophalangeal joint
• tops of toes in a tight shoe
inv: positioning works only if it is
tx: Treat EARLY and often to avoid surgery
• wider toe box · positioning if flexible

head: h
Morton's neuroma
common digital nerve fibrosis, usually 3rd-4th metatarsal space
tx: Lower heel · wider, taller toe box
• metatarsal pad in a foot orthosis

head: h
Diabetic foot
neuropathy + poor blood flow
ulcer in 15% of people with diabetes
inv: • occlusion: pain, pallor, paresthesia, paralysis, pulselessness
tx: debridement or amputation may be needed
